grc:pron:τῇσιν.gloss: feminine dative plural of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun) and ὅ (hó, relative pronoun) with movable nu

grc:other:Β.gloss: The letter beta (βῆτα), the second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:β.gloss: Lower-case beta (βῆτα), the second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiced bilabial plosive: /b/ and later the voiced labiodental fricative /v/. It is preceded by α and followed by γ.

grc:verb:ἔστω.gloss: third-person singular present active imperative of εἰμί (eimí): let her/him/it be!

grc:verb:ἁμαρτάνουσιν.gloss: masculine/neuter dative plural of ᾰ̔μᾰρτᾰ́νων (hămărtắnōn) with movable nu

grc:verb:γέγραπται.gloss: third-person singular perfect middle/passive indicative of γράφω (gráphō)

grc:verb:χρῆται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative/subjunctive of χράομαι (khráomai, “to use”)

grc:verb:ἔργοις.gloss: second-person singular present active optative of ἔργω (érgō)

grc:verb:ποιεῖται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative contracted of ποιέω (poiéō)

grc:pron:νώ.gloss: we two; both of us; us two

grc:verb:ἔτυχε.gloss: third-person singular aorist active indicative of τῠγχᾰ́νω (tŭnkhắnō)

grc:verb:ἔτυχεν.gloss: third-person singular aorist active indicative of τῠγχᾰ́νω (tŭnkhắnō) with movable nu

grc:adj:δυσόριστος.gloss: difficult to adapt to a limit

grc:verb:λεχθέντων.gloss: third-person plural aorist passive imperative of λέγω (légō)

grc:conj:οὔθ'.gloss: apocopic form of οὔτε (oúte) used before vowel or diphthong with rough breathing

grc:verb:ποιοῦσιν.gloss: contracted third-person plural present active indicative of ποιέω (poiéō)

grc:verb:λείπεται.gloss: third-person singular present middle/passive indicative of λείπω (leípō)

grc:verb:θεωρήσωμεν.gloss: first-person plural aorist active subjunctive of θεωρέω (theōréō)

grc:conj:ἄρ.gloss: alternative form of ᾰ̓́ρᾰ (ắră, “so; then; therefore; consequently”) before a consonant

grc:conj:ἄρ'.gloss: apocopic form of ᾰ̓́ρᾰ (ắră, “so; then; therefore; consequently”)

grc:noun:μέσῳ.gloss: dative singular of μέσος (mésos) and μέσον (méson)

grc:noun:εὐθεῖα.gloss: ellipsis of εὐθεῖα πτῶσις (eutheîa ptôsis, “nominative case”, literally “straight case”)

grc:other:α.gloss: Lower-case alpha (ἄλφα), the first letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the open front or central unrounded vowel /a/. It is followed by β.

grc:other:Α.gloss: The letter ἄλφα (álpha, “alpha”), the first letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:υ.gloss: Lower-case upsilon (ὖ ψιλόν), the 20th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the close back rounded vowel /u/ and later the close front rounded vowel /y/. It is preceded by τ and followed by φ.

grc:other:Υ.gloss: The letter now called upsilon (ὖ ψιλόν (û psilón)), the 20th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:part:πω.gloss: up to this time, yet (as a negative polarity item)

grc:verb:ἤλθομεν.gloss: first-person plural aorist active indicative of ἔρχομαι (érkhomai)

grc:other:Ψ.gloss: The letter psi (ψεῖ), the 23rd letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:ψ.gloss: Lower-case psi (ψεῖ), the 23rd letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the consonant cluster /ps/ in the Eastern Greek alphabet and the voiceless aspirated velar plosive /kʰ/ in the Western Greek alphabet (compare Etruscan 𐌙 (χ) khe). It is preceded by χ and followed by ω.

grc:other:Κ.gloss: The letter kappa (κάππα), the tenth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:part:κ'.gloss: apocopic form of κε (ke) (used before the smooth breathing)

grc:part:χ'.gloss: apocopic form of κε (ke) (used before the rough breathing)

grc:other:Φ.gloss: The letter phi (φεῖ), the 21st letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:φ.gloss: Lower-case phi (φεῖ), the 21st letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiceless aspirated bilabial plosive /pʰ/ and later the voiceless labiodental fricative /f/. It is preceded by υ and followed by χ.

grc:verb:ὑπάρξουσι.gloss: third-person plural future active indicative of ὑπάρχω (hupárkhō)

grc:verb:ὑπάρξουσιν.gloss: third-person plural future active indicative of ὑπάρχω (hupárkhō)

grc:verb:λεγόντων.gloss: third-person plural present active imperative of λέγω (légō)

grc:name:Χθών.gloss: the Earth, personified as a goddess

grc:adj:αὐτόματος.gloss: acting of one's own will, of oneself

grc:adj:ἁμός.gloss: ἁμός (A) or ἀμός [α], ή , όν , Aeol. ἄμμος A, No.

grc:verb:ἠνέχθη.gloss: third-person singular aorist passive indicative of φέρω (phérō)

grc:adv:πολλάκι.gloss: Epic form of πολλᾰ́κῐς (pollắkĭs, “often, many times”)

grc:verb:δύω.gloss: to cause to sink; to plunge

grc:adj:τριπλάσιος.gloss: thrice as many, thrice as much, thrice as great as

grc:verb:ἐνέσται.gloss: third-person singular future middle indicative of ἔνειμι (éneimi)

grc:verb:θεωρήσομεν.gloss: first-person plural future active indicative of θεωρέω (theōréō)

grc:name:Σωκράτης.gloss: a male given name, equivalent to English Socrates

grc:verb:θεωροῦμεν.gloss: contracted first-person plural present active indicative of θεωρέω (theōréō)

grc:other:ἅπασιν.gloss: masculine/neuter dative plural of ᾰ̔́πᾱς (hắpās) with movable nu

grc:verb:ἔθω.gloss: to be accustomed, to be wont

grc:verb:εἴωθα.gloss: to be accustomed, to tend to

grc:noun:κλίνη.gloss: that on which one lies, couch

grc:verb:παραλείπω.gloss: leave on one side, leave remaining

grc:noun:περίοδος.gloss: one who goes the rounds, patrol

grc:verb:ἀφίστημι.gloss: put away, remove, keep out of the way

grc:verb:ἔμενεν.gloss: third-person singular imperfect active indicative of μένω (ménō)

grc:adv:μηδαμῶς.gloss: By no means, in no way, not at all

grc:verb:λαμβάνομεν.gloss: first-person plural present active indicative of λαμβάνω (lambánō)

grc:verb:ἐφάνη.gloss: third-person singular aorist passive indicative of φαίνω (phaínō)

grc:name:Οὐρανός.gloss: Uranus, a primordial god in Greek mythology

grc:name:Ὥρα.gloss: one of the Horae or Hours in Greek mythology; a Hora or Hour

grc:noun:ὥρη.gloss: Epic and Ionic form of ὥρᾱ (hṓrā)

grc:name:Πατήρ.gloss: God the Father; (one of the three Persons of the Trinity)
